Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 28, "heading": "CHAPTER 26. I FALL INTO CAPTIVITY", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u028-b0046", "target": "Утро было прекрасное, раннее, и я решил пойти прогуляться по одной из тех аллей под проволочными арками и предаться своей страсти, размышляя о её образе. Проходя через холл, я встретил её собачку, которую звали Джип — сокращённо от Джипси. Я приблизился к нему нежно, ибо любил даже его; но он показал весь набор зубов, залез под стул нарочно, чтобы зарычать оттуда, и не желал слышать о малейшей фамильярности.", "source_sha256": "87845223cab8ddd95aab25b712620a16a995fb66066ede7fe9a73a9cb3f1f0e4", "target_id": "ru-en85-u028-b0046", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "6dee9c1fd1495ce42b7a79720b35435895269c2b79c33965740854906f06e8ee"}, {"source_id": "en85-u028-b0047", "target": "Сад был прохладен и безлюден. Я бродил, гадая, каковы были бы мои чувства счастья, если бы я мог когда-нибудь обручиться с этим дорогим чудом. Что до брака, состояния и всего такого, я думаю, я был тогда почти так же невинно бескорыстен, как когда любил маленькую Эмили. Быть допущенным называть её «Дорой», писать ей, обожать её и боготворить, иметь основание думать, что, когда она с другими людьми, она всё же помнит обо мне, казалось мне вершиной человеческих устремлений — я уверен, что это была вершина моих. Нет сомнения, что я был томный молодой болванчик; но во всём этом была чистота сердца, которая мешает мне вспоминать об этом с полным презрением, как бы я ни смеялся.", "source_sha256": "4a004d2e41d737d240e189d3415813173dfdfc18e93b204caba6a707d71fd45b", "target_id": "ru-en85-u028-b0047", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "7f8e6ae906bcf715fdd6672020d5d1300bd1bddeea4a7e995d47bd004d48f057"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 26, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u028-b0048", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I had not been walking long, when I turned a corner, and met her. I tingle again from head to foot as my recollection turns that corner, and my pen shakes in my hand.", "sha256": "41c459f6c7ed71294aec7f9fb5fe19cfc883e896fa6aa704bce61604be66d48d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[49]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0049", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You—are—out early, Miss Spenlow,’ said I.", "sha256": "9334260e489d7662bba4457a7a2dd06f6d451089683dee7152dc2cdf469979de", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[50]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0050", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘It’s so stupid at home,’ she replied, ‘and Miss Murdstone is so absurd! She talks such nonsense about its being necessary for the day to be aired, before I come out. Aired!’ (She laughed, here, in the most melodious manner.) ‘On a Sunday morning, when I don’t practise, I must do something. So I told papa last night I must come out. Besides, it’s the brightest time of the whole day. Don’t you think so?’", "sha256": "920a27936e457fcc76f0352049482d95fb1df6d88549f75c174bcec48a84306c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[51]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0051", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I hazarded a bold flight, and said (not without stammering) that it was very bright to me then, though it had been very dark to me a minute before.", "sha256": "7b266aad05185e4ba26aebd38ae375a3d0f6fe5331e91dc81929b54f7ce33f46", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[52]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0052", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Do you mean a compliment?’ said Dora, ‘or that the weather has really changed?’", "sha256": "a23a0ecb0f75dd04786edc3a22157164161af401f78d11449661664883de20f6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[53]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0053", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I stammered worse than before, in replying that I meant no compliment, but the plain truth; though I was not aware of any change having taken place in the weather. It was in the state of my own feelings, I added bashfully: to clench the explanation.", "sha256": "0293d241610a0121fe473da83f5a928a0a8bd55f15f7910e47d887ef1c4b2848", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[54]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0054", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I never saw such curls—how could I, for there never were such curls!—as those she shook out to hide her blushes. As to the straw hat and blue ribbons which was on the top of the curls, if I could only have hung it up in my room in Buckingham Street, what a priceless possession it would have been!", "sha256": "bd520e0227dd468d3c5c73e7cbb7133bef15b357d4c97f57dc5101e0b29dbc7a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[55]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0055", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You have just come home from Paris,’ said I.", "sha256": "dc15a314993f2d5d75117418ba1e4c5248834e2d282604e6de2ad820fb793e08", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[56]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0056", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Yes,’ said she. ‘Have you ever been there?’", "sha256": "14a115b65025d97003f0f7abe260e34ec93f19faa52e9e7998c856f5e0740525", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[57]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0057", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No.’", "sha256": "2bdf78717dff75748376e7bf00029aed95c88e280ab52148149726890e89781e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[58]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0058", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh! I hope you’ll go soon! You would like it so much!’", "sha256": "65f73f5225cc1f0f17791fac629d0c361194963feb0056e03c69269aed65ec9e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[59]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0059", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Traces of deep-seated anguish appeared in my countenance. That she should hope I would go, that she should think it possible I could go, was insupportable. I depreciated Paris; I depreciated France. I said I wouldn’t leave England, under existing circumstances, for any earthly consideration. Nothing should induce me. In short, she was shaking the curls again, when the little dog came running along the walk to our relief.", "sha256": "75937b7af633b34cd7a7a6425764403a82b5217970586f23a0a52e9ba5a67b33", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[60]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0060", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He was mortally jealous of me, and persisted in barking at me. She took him up in her arms—oh my goodness!—and caressed him, but he persisted upon barking still. He wouldn’t let me touch him, when I tried; and then she beat him. It increased my sufferings greatly to see the pats she gave him for punishment on the bridge of his blunt nose, while he winked his eyes, and licked her hand, and still growled within himself like a little double-bass. At length he was quiet—well he might be with her dimpled chin upon his head!—and we walked away to look at a greenhouse.", "sha256": "03238f4d82d53055b3a234a66d445074cdb26a7c0af1eb5761868c263f581d37", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[61]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0061", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You are not very intimate with Miss Murdstone, are you?’ said Dora. —‘My pet.’", "sha256": "826c1c1e6431ddef139de6cfcae33b4756747b745702e02a217b08f033f89d9e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[62]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0062", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "(The two last words were to the dog. Oh, if they had only been to me!)", "sha256": "1ea3836c7033c309a4e272779bfd081c3446a62669b67ef32efd7a6556e5ed12", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[63]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0063", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No,’ I replied. ‘Not at all so.’", "sha256": "e51a9f3e80191f3a374c668ea2b8fc52035f455f30818ebbcc7f71400698dcc1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[64]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0064", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘She is a tiresome creature,’ said Dora, pouting. ‘I can’t think what papa can have been about, when he chose such a vexatious thing to be my companion. Who wants a protector? I am sure I don’t want a protector. Jip can protect me a great deal better than Miss Murdstone,—can’t you, Jip, dear?’", "sha256": "91d34a72c856a3ffc393302129f972d6b92f4e326b719d09e564c2990b2b6a2c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[65]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0065", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He only winked lazily, when she kissed his ball of a head.", "sha256": "7ddb1b1ae3888ab32120bb57e3eff4bb24049cd9bee24f597990c4c2301b9178", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[66]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0066", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Papa calls her my confidential friend, but I am sure she is no such thing—is she, Jip? We are not going to confide in any such cross people, Jip and I. We mean to bestow our confidence where we like, and to find out our own friends, instead of having them found out for us—don’t we, Jip?’", "sha256": "520e5ca454561dcc07ca95eb13fa23bc06fd5d7a0a175489eea3c5b10ebceda8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[67]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0067", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Jip made a comfortable noise, in answer, a little like a tea-kettle when it sings. As for me, every word was a new heap of fetters, riveted above the last.", "sha256": "86c32cf3806c59201b4f6a3afd2211a3a99cd83c85c74b2a713dc890df468075", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[68]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0068", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘It is very hard, because we have not a kind Mama, that we are to have, instead, a sulky, gloomy old thing like Miss Murdstone, always following us about—isn’t it, Jip? Never mind, Jip. We won’t be confidential, and we’ll make ourselves as happy as we can in spite of her, and we’ll tease her, and not please her—won’t we, Jip?’", "sha256": "1c3657514ab9fb68ce88de783c5043cf7bc3efd0c5736c69ef2af4934ce9addd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[69]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0069", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "If it had lasted any longer, I think I must have gone down on my knees on the gravel, with the probability before me of grazing them, and of being presently ejected from the premises besides. But, by good fortune the greenhouse was not far off, and these words brought us to it.", "sha256": "64d5b70e94d52b6ef6773288e7dcf8b541ace1fd83b62eb9872097dc601c1c86", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[70]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0070", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "It contained quite a show of beautiful geraniums. We loitered along in front of them, and Dora often stopped to admire this one or that one, and I stopped to admire the same one, and Dora, laughing, held the dog up childishly, to smell the flowers; and if we were not all three in Fairyland, certainly I was. The scent of a geranium leaf, at this day, strikes me with a half comical half serious wonder as to what change has come over me in a moment; and then I see a straw hat and blue ribbons, and a quantity of curls, and a little black dog being held up, in two slender arms, against a bank of blossoms and bright leaves.", "sha256": "b5cbbe34b79ddb0590c64d6696d519a9d8f132af1859bbbf2ab4d0bcd884be1c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[71]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0071", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Miss Murdstone had been looking for us. She found us here; and presented her uncongenial cheek, the little wrinkles in it filled with hair powder, to Dora to be kissed. Then she took Dora’s arm in hers, and marched us into breakfast as if it were a soldier’s funeral.", "sha256": "3ccd8d51f61eda35f5e8246042e5ab6346c8a3e88ae967fe972e513d459b52aa", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[72]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0072", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "How many cups of tea I drank, because Dora made it, I don’t know. But, I perfectly remember that I sat swilling tea until my whole nervous system, if I had had any in those days, must have gone by the board. By and by we went to church. Miss Murdstone was between Dora and me in the pew; but I heard her sing, and the congregation vanished. A sermon was delivered—about Dora, of course—and I am afraid that is all I know of the service.", "sha256": "c31af62c005377807a22b7e3a0440aa6d3de63da3f93ae31b282d812760e59ea", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[73]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0073", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We had a quiet day. No company, a walk, a family dinner of four, and an evening of looking over books and pictures; Miss Murdstone with a homily before her, and her eye upon us, keeping guard vigilantly. Ah! little did Mr. Spenlow imagine, when he sat opposite to me after dinner that day, with his pocket-handkerchief over his head, how fervently I was embracing him, in my fancy, as his son-in-law! Little did he think, when I took leave of him at night, that he had just given his full consent to my being engaged to Dora, and that I was invoking blessings on his head!", "sha256": "1b85a502bd699f7cc5a0af66c4adb663d2e9e6a64e98694342ebf023841f2e88", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[74]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0074", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "We departed early in the morning, for we had a Salvage case coming on in the Admiralty Court, requiring a rather accurate knowledge of the whole science of navigation, in which (as we couldn’t be expected to know much about those matters in the Commons) the judge had entreated two old Trinity Masters, for charity’s sake, to come and help him out. Dora was at the breakfast-table to make the tea again, however; and I had the melancholy pleasure of taking off my hat to her in the phaeton, as she stood on the door-step with Jip in her arms.", "sha256": "fd39cc10f11cc02a272119fa85cec70922c0067c22ea4a157297c483ccdda3df", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[75]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0075", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "What the Admiralty was to me that day; what nonsense I made of our case in my mind, as I listened to it; how I saw ‘DORA’ engraved upon the blade of the silver oar which they lay upon the table, as the emblem of that high jurisdiction; and how I felt when Mr. Spenlow went home without me (I had had an insane hope that he might take me back again), as if I were a mariner myself, and the ship to which I belonged had sailed away and left me on a desert island; I shall make no fruitless effort to describe. If that sleepy old court could rouse itself, and present in any visible form the daydreams I have had in it about Dora, it would reveal my truth.", "sha256": "866f59fbdb2d91081461cc38955db1d3d90916a161da62672550974eeae786fa", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[76]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0076", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I don’t mean the dreams that I dreamed on that day alone, but day after day, from week to week, and term to term. I went there, not to attend to what was going on, but to think about Dora. If ever I bestowed a thought upon the cases, as they dragged their slow length before me, it was only to wonder, in the matrimonial cases (remembering Dora), how it was that married people could ever be otherwise than happy; and, in the Prerogative cases, to consider, if the money in question had been left to me, what were the foremost steps I should immediately have taken in regard to Dora. Within the first week of my passion, I bought four sumptuous waistcoats—not for myself; I had no pride in them; for Dora—and took to wearing straw-coloured kid gloves in the streets, and laid the foundations of all the corns I have ever had. If the boots I wore at that period could only be produced and compared with the natural size of my feet, they would show what the state of my heart was, in a most affecting manner.", "sha256": "cbe6be15897a9a633449f0d8bfef8418f7b40d0d8f2ae8776447f3600de6ba26", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[77]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u028-b0077", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "And yet, wretched cripple as I made myself by this act of homage to Dora, I walked miles upon miles daily in the hope of seeing her. Not only was I soon as well known on the Norwood Road as the postmen on that beat, but I pervaded London likewise. I walked about the streets where the best shops for ladies were, I haunted the Bazaar like an unquiet spirit, I fagged through the Park again and again, long after I was quite knocked up. Sometimes, at long intervals and on rare occasions, I saw her. Perhaps I saw her glove waved in a carriage window; perhaps I met her, walked with her and Miss Murdstone a little way, and spoke to her. In the latter case I was always very miserable afterwards, to think that I had said nothing to the purpose; or that she had no idea of the extent of my devotion, or that she cared nothing about me. I was always looking out, as may be supposed, for another invitation to Mr. Spenlow’s house.
